images.title: A fold parallel to a diagonal
images.purpose: Show that folding one corner onto the centre gives a crease parallel to the diagonal.
images.composition: One large square sheet centred, with the diagonal, the crease and the folded corner; four short labels.
exact_structure: A square sheet with a thin dark outline.
A teal (#0072B2) diagonal from the top left corner to the bottom right corner.
A grey (#6B7280) dashed second diagonal from the bottom left corner to the top right corner, passing through the centre dot.
The top right corner shown as a reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot with a curved arrow going to the centre dot of the sheet.
An amber (#E69F00) crease that joins the midpoint of the top edge to the midpoint of the right edge; it crosses the dashed diagonal at a right angle, marked with a small square.
Both the teal diagonal and the amber crease carry matching double arrow marks to show they are parallel.
rejection: crease not joining the midpoints of the top and right edges
crease not parallel to the teal diagonal
images.takeaway: A fold that puts a corner on the centre makes a crease parallel to the diagonal.
images.description: A square sheet with a diagonal, a dashed second diagonal and an amber crease parallel to the first diagonal.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students follow the corner to the centre and see the crease runs the same way as the diagonal.

image_decisions.why: The fold that gives a parallel line is the key move.
